1Print method

Start here — pick how your design will be printed. This sets your minimum and how your price is worked out.

Screen printing is the standard — minimum 24. Its prices are the print fees for the product you picked.

2Your artwork

This is where your logo comes from. Upload it here and it lands on the item above.

Add your logo

Tap the big gold button above to upload your logo — it will appear on your item.

Your comment is included in the design summary in step 11.

PNG, JPG, or SVG, up to 20 MB. A transparent PNG works best. Have the original in AI, PSD, or PDF? Attach it too — that’s the file production would print from.

The shop asks for the original file too — please attach the AI, PSD, or PDF original above before you finish.

3Product

Tap the item you want printed — the preview picture changes to match.

Hat style — 5-panel trucker

One size — adjustable snapback. Hats print on the front panel only, and the minimum is 12 hats.

T-shirts use real photos, aprons use your own photos in denim, khaki, and white, and hats use generated front-view preview photos — mesh and closed 5-panel trucker styles — in white, black, navy, grey, and red. Polos, long sleeves, and hoodies use generated blank preview photos — every color (white, black, navy, grey, and red) has its own preview photo, front and back, with the garment in that color and the background white, so every color shows the moment you tap it. Generated previews are not your actual products: swap in real photos of those items before anything goes live.

About this item

4Print location

Pick where this design goes — front, back, or a small pocket print. Each one can hold its own artwork.

Print one location or all three — each side keeps its own artwork, size, and position.

5Shirt color

Tap a color to see it on the item right away. Logo color is right below it.

Logo color

Current: original colors

Pick a color and your logo is recolored right on your item. This works best on single-color logos like black lettering — a full-color photo or detailed artwork will turn into one flat color. If your file has a solid background, remove the background first (in step 6 below) so only the logo itself changes color.

6Artwork size & background removal

Fine-tune the logo on this side: slide to make it bigger or smaller, and clean off a background if your file has one.

SmallerBigger

Background removal

Uploaded a logo that came with a background — a white box around it, for example? Remove it here so just the logo sits on your item.

GentleStronger

How it works: it removes the background that’s connected to the edges of the picture, following its shade as it goes — so a solid white or solid-color background comes off cleanly, even with uneven light or a soft shadow across it. Busy photo backgrounds won’t cut out cleanly here — for those, the original file (AI / PSD / PDF) is what production would use.

7Print size

How large the print can be — Standard fits most designs.

Pocket prints are up to 4″ × 4″.

8Sizes & quantities

Type how many you need of each size — or tap the − and + buttons under each box. The sizes all add together toward the 24 minimum: 6 in every size makes 30, and that counts.

Minimum order: 24 items — aprons are minimum 24, and screen printing is minimum 24. After 24, order as many as you want — there’s no maximum.

Aprons are one size — just enter how many you need. Minimum 24 aprons for screen printing.

Total: 0 items

9Bringing your own garment?

Optional — only tick the box if you’re bringing your own garments for us to print on.

Tick this box if you’re supplying the garments yourself. You won’t be charged for the garment at all — you only pay for the printing. Keep using the product and color above to preview how your design will look; the sizes & quantities in step 8 are still the counts we’ll print.

Where to ship your garment: After we receive your order, we’ll email you where to ship your garment. No shipping address is shown here — we keep it private and email it to you once your order comes in, so please don’t ship anything until you get that email.

After we receive your order, we’ll email you where to ship your garment at this address. Your email is included in your design summary in step 11.
